sources.subject: Re: Confirmation of Steel Material Origin for Rack Cabinet
sources.evidence:
EVIDENCE CHECK — cited quotes are genuine. In /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lanstar-mail2/752f8fc5-be77-4ab5-bb66-347588e328d1/scratchpad/retry_packets/r_025.json the thread is verbatim as claimed: kyu@lanstar.co.kr to guzhiyi@bor-cable.com, 2026-02-09 06:10 UTC, "the customer is asking whether the steel material is imported from Russia... please stamp your company seal on the attached file"; Gu returns the sealed "Rack Cabinet.pdf" at 07:28 the same day. Issuer is Xiangshan Bor International Trade Co., Ltd / Ningbo Borland Electronic Co., Ltd. The PDF text covers "our Rack Cabinet products" and "cold-rolled steel sheets, structural steel components, and related metal parts" — a line-wide materials-origin declaration, no individual model named. Supplier identity and product category are certain, and there is no product-type mismatch to exploit (this is not a performance test tied to a specific construction, shielding or connector).

WHY IT STILL FAILS — the family list is arbitrarily truncated, and the stated rationale is factually wrong. The claim says it lists "the rack-cabinet families the Lanstar catalogue explicitly attributes to BOR", but family_catalog.json attributes many more cabinet families to BOR just as explicitly, all omitted:
- LS-300H/LS-300HB — catalogue text literally reads "LS-300H, LS-300HB BOR 사양서"
- LS-500H/LS-500HB — "LS-500H, LS-500HB BOR 사양서"; LS-500HS — "LS-500HS BOR 캐비닛 사양서"
These come from the very same 2023-12-26 spec batch the claim cites for LS-750H/LS-1000H/LS-1200H~LS-2000H, so the inclusion boundary is inconsistent on its own terms.
- LS-300HN, LS-300HR, LS-1600HC, LS-1800HC, LS-1800HBS-NOS are further BOR cabinet families.
- The HS series (LS-1200HS/1600HS/1800HS/2000HS) was presumably dropped because the catalogue labels it "Jiasheng 랙 캐비닛 사양서". That is a trap: Jiasheng is BOR's own cabinet factory. Document sha1 8d6d48fee37a84ab9bc12c22a0c45de1ff8a0b08 carries issuer "BOR International Trade Co., Ltd (Xiangshan/Ningbo, 중국) — Jiasheng 캐비닛 공장 도면", and the HS drawing (sha1 f3f6b0e4cd4274b95e6e4a9d9b32c205422d30ea) arrived from guzhiyi@bor-cable.com.
- The HQ 601S series (sha1 afea5d9eda9264f07c4ec6f80e9cc3654774c748, "BOR 제공, 2023-07-03") and the HSQ VE series (sha1 083e7a05ea6bceb135a57c31ae5227090027510e) likewise both trace to guzhiyi@bor-cable.com.

DECISIVE CORROBORATION — two BOR-issued lineup documents settle the scope:
1. sha1 88bac53ac3e0a920f251db213244a495a470388a, issuer "Xiangshan Bor International Trade Co., Ltd" — "BOR 캐비닛 사양 비교표(Excel)", received 2026-03, one month AFTER this declaration, scope_target "완제품 캐비닛 전 라인업": LS-240HC, LS-300H, LS-300HN, LS-300HR, LS-500H, LS-500HS, LS-750H, LS-750HS, LS-1000H, LS-1200H, LS-1200HS, LS-1600H, LS-1600HC, LS-1800H, LS-1800HS, LS-1800HC, LS-1800HBS, LS-1800HBS-NOS, LS-2000H, LS-2000HS.
2. sha1 1d00d683724a7be0a7083e32866bb25ee886038e (duplicate 78ceec76074d1dc0d68daea592a00e225886b394), issuer "Xiangshan Bor / Ningbo Borland (guzhiyi@bor-cable.com)" — 机柜配件明细表 lock/key table, 2023-11, listing the same 20-model cabinet range.
The claim named 15 families; BOR's own line-wide roster is roughly 38 once the HB colour variants documented in the BOR spec sheets are counted.

UNIQUENESS TEST — the "would a different family fit equally well?" question inverts here. The problem is not that a rival family fits better; it is that this is a whole-line declaration and the proposed list under-covers it. A customer asking about LS-300H, LS-500HS, LS-1800HS or LS-1600HC would be wrongly told no declaration exists, even though BOR's sealed statement covers them.

DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS — the 2-post open racks (LS-1600HO/HBO, LS-1800HO/HBO, LS-2000HO/HBO) also came from guzhiyi@bor-cable.com and are SPCC steel, but the declaration's own wording is "our Rack Cabinet products" / "the rack cabinets manufactured by our company"; an open 2-post frame is not a cabinet, so extending it there would misrepresent the document. Same reasoning excludes BOR-made steel rack accessories (LS-SHE-* / LS-SSHE-* shelves, LS-HS2FAN/LS-HS4FAN fan units, LS-EPLB-48P19 patch panel, LS-PB1x point boxes). LS-1000HS appears in the 2023-11 BOR lock table but is not a catalogue family key, so it is omitted.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY — the HQ (601S) and HSQ (VE) series do not appear in the 2026-03 "전 라인업" table, so they may be superseded by the declaration date; they are retained because they are BOR-supplied cabinets and the declaration is line-wide rather than model-specific. Everything else in the revised list is backed by BOR's own roster documents. [검증-수정]

sources.evidence: 본 메일(INBOX:15816, 2024-07-12)에서 kyu는 "If you have CE sheet for Cabinet, Please send it"라고만 요청했고 BOR(guzhiyi@bor-cable.com)는 "Attached certificates and test reports are for Jiasheng cabinets"라고 회신 — 즉 이 인증서는 'Jiasheng이 만든 랜스타 캐비닛'의 CE 근거 문서다. sources.subject: ROHS for cable
sources.evidence:
CITED EVIDENCE VERIFIED BY FILE HASH. shasum -a 1 on the raw attachments gives 757538761d61f6ee8476e3745492035576372d70 (505,746 B) for ALL of: attachments_raw/INBOX_7401/HDPE-ROHS-2020.PDF, INBOX_7475/HDPE-ROHS-2020.PDF, INBOX_7890/HDPE-ROHS-2020.PDF, and INBOX_5438/HDPE-ROHS.PDF. (a) INBOX:7475 2022-06-20 "300M Roll - RoHS": kyu "1. LS-5SFTP-300M 2. LS-6SFTP-300M", Gu "The material of SF/UTP Cat.5e/6 are CCA conductor, HDPE insulation, Al-Mylar shielding, ALMG braiding, PVC jacket" — exactly as claimed. (b) INBOX:7890 2022-08-15 "Re: Data sheet - LS-5FTPSD-BKXm": Gu "2) Insulation: HDPE" — exactly as claimed. Both links stand.

WHY REVISE — OMITTED MODEL WITH STRONGER EVIDENCE THAN ANY IN THE CLAIM: a fourth mail, INBOX:5438 (2021-09-30, "Re: RE: Dust cap"), carries the byte-identical file (renamed HDPE-ROHS.PDF) in direct answer to kyu's 2021-09-30 request naming "LS-DC-RJ45PP-WHC / LS-DC-USBPE-WHC", with Gu writing "LS-DC-RJ45PP-WHC is just one material: PP and LS-DC-USBPE-WHC is also just one material: HDPE" (the PP sibling file 917809a3… goes to the RJ45PP cap). For that dust cap the report is effectively a whole-product RoHS, not a component report, and a scan of kb_docs shows this sha1 is the ONLY RoHS document in the archive attached to LS-DC-USBPE-WHC — omitting it leaves that model with zero RoHS evidence. The prior pass (kb_docs.json) already had it; the claim dropped it. Added to both models and families.

USB FAMILIES — RETAINED, BUT THIS IS THE INFERENTIAL TIER. The packet's own thread INBOX:7401 (2022-06-10) is genuinely generic: kyu "test report or COC (CE) report about USB2.0 cable", Gu "USB 2.0 Cable material is easy, including conductor(copper wire), insulation(HDPE), shielding 1(Al-Mylar), shielding 2(ALMG braiding), jacket(PVC)"; no LS/LSP/LSN/ZOT code anywhere, and the same-day sibling INBOX:7400 is the connector-only set. The BOR USB 2.0 datasheets corroborate the construction: LS-USB-AMAF-xxM.pdf / LS-USB-AMAM-xxM.pdf / LS-USB-AMBM-xxM.pdf all read "USB 2.0 CABLE, 7/0.12BC*1P+7/0.12BC*2C+AL+48/0.12ALMG+PVC, OD 4.5MM" with a labelled INSULATION item in the material list, and LS-USB MINI 5P-xM.pdf (internal code LS-USB-AM5P) the same at OD 4.0MM. The claim enumerates the whole BOR USB 2.0 cable set rather than picking one arbitrarily, so it does not fail the "another family fits equally well" test. Two corrections: (1) the INBOX:3885 corroboration is construction-only — the HDPE report sent there for LS-USB2.0-AMAF-sXm is a DIFFERENT file, sha1 49f6ef6f34515d454f0e51ae33a0709468f6c8da, which kb_docs already maps to LS-USB2.0-AMAF-SXM; so 757538 on that family is a later-revision duplicate, not a first link; (2) including LS-USB2.0-AMAF-SXM while excluding its same-series siblings is inconsistent — added LS-USB2.0-AMAF-S5M (members_of lists it separately; PFAS report 8e1cb60a groups it with LS-5FTPSD-BK5M). Did not add "USB2.0-AMAF-S1M" because it lacks an LS/LSP/LSN/ZOT prefix.

DOCUMENT NATURE / DELIVERY CAVEAT: the PDF is a compounder blanket report — applicant GUANGZHOU KINGSENS POLYMER SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY, sample "Polyolefins / White translucent grains", SGS Sample ID CAN20-195783.002, and page 4 REMARK lists ~100 KS-series resin grades (KS 5010BK, KS 1010G, KS L410, KS 7100-7310 …). No Lanstar or BOR name appears in it. It therefore can only ever be linked by "which model-named request did the supplier answer with this exact file", which is the four threads above. It must be served as a raw-material (insulation) RoHS + halogen (EN 14582, F/Cl/Br/I ND) supporting document, never as a finished-product certificate, and its 2020-11-12 date should be disclosed.

NOT ADDED, FLAGGED FOR THE PARENT: family_catalog also contains LS-CAT.5E-SFTP-300M and LS-CAT.6-SFTP-300M, whose 2023-06-26 BOR spec sheets describe the same cable as LS-5SFTP-300M / LS-6SFTP-300M (4P, CCA solid 1/0.50 24AWG, "절연 HDPE" 0.88 / 1.00 mm, AL foil + Mylar, AL-MG 80/0.12 braid, PVC). They are probably naming aliases and would be equally valid targets, but no request in the archive names them with this file, so I left them out rather than widen the tag on inference. sources.evidence:
CORE LINK VERIFIED (models unchanged). attach_map.json + bodies.json confirm the identical file (sha1 994ab8ea…, 'AL-Mylar- ROHS.pdf', 559203 B) is attached to BOTH INBOX:7401 (2022-06-10 'ROHS for cable', USB 2.0) and INBOX:7475 (2022-06-20 '300M Roll - RoHS'). In 7475 kyu's request reads verbatim "Could you please send RoHS sheet? 1. LS-5SFTP-300M 2. LS-6SFTP-300M" and Gu answers "The material of SF/UTP Cat.5e/6 are CCA condcutor, HDPE insulation, Al-Mylar shielding, ALMG braiding, PVC jacket" — a direct thread_request link. Corroborated by the LS-5SFTP-300M BOR spec (SF/UTP Cat.5e, CCA solid 24AWG, HDPE, shield "AL Foil 22*0.025 + Mylar", AL-MG braid, PVC) and by identical treatment of the four sibling raw-material reports from the same mail (CCA-ROHS 495ac714, HDPE-ROHS-2020 75753876, PVC-ROHS2.0 18f10e67, ALMG-ROHS cb7707e1 — all carry LS-5SFTP-300M/LS-6SFTP-300M).

USB SIDE PARTLY HOLDS. INBOX:7401 is itself a genuine thread_request: kyu asks for a test report/COC for "USB2.0 cable", Gu replies "USB 2.0 Cable material is easy, including conductor(copper wire), insulation(HDPE), shielding 1(Al-Mylar), shielding 2(ALMG braiding), jacket(PVC)" and attaches this file — so the generic→family mapping is legitimate, and it is bounded, not a guess: INBOX:5040 (2021-08-18) Gu sends "the data sheet for all USB 2.0 cables" = exactly LS-USB-AMAF-xxM.pdf, LS-USB-AMAM-xxM.pdf, LS-USB-AMBM-xxM.pdf. I read the AMBM drawing text directly: "USB 2.0 CABLE, 7/0.12BC*1P+7/0.12BC*2C+AL+48/0.12ALMG+PVC, OD: 4.5MM" with MATERIAL LIST entry AL-FOIL; AMAF/AMAM/AM5P catalogue entries carry the same string ("7/0.12BC×1P + 7/0.12BC×2C + AL 포일 + 48/0.12 ALMG 편조 + PVC"). USB 3.0 families (LS-USB3.0-AMAF/AMAM/AMBM/AMMIC, LS-U3AOC*) share the 7/0.12BC construction but are excluded by the mail's explicit "USB 2.0", so the four-family set is specific.

REFUTED ELEMENT — LS-USB2.0-AMAF-SXM removed. It is BOR's separate "USB screw cable" line and already holds its OWN complete raw-material RoHS package from its own explicitly-model-named thread INBOX:3885 (2021-03-23, kyu: "We need ROHS sheet for LS-USB2.0-AMAF-sXm series"; Gu: "SGS report of conductor, HDPE, Al Foil, Braiding, PVC, screws"), including a DIFFERENT aluminium-foil report Al Foil-RoHS.pdf (sha1 41b4f848…, SGS SHAEC1803726201, 2018-03-07, HUBEI PLUTO ELECTRONICS) — whereas this doc is CTI A2220181751101001C (2022-05-14, 湖北亿田鑫). SXM was not among the "all USB 2.0 cables" datasheets, and its family_catalog entry contains no cable construction at all (only BCTC2212541532C/R, a male/female screw-extension RoHS cert that equally covers RJ45/HDMI/DP/mDP/USB-C), so the claim's catalogue-construction argument does not apply to it. Attaching this report to SXM would hand a customer a different foil lot's certificate when a better-evidenced one exists. The sibling family key USB2.0-AMAF-S1M is excluded for the same reason.

Optional note (not added, inference only): family_catalog also contains LS-CAT.5E-SFTP-300M / LS-CAT.6-SFTP-300M (2023-06-26 BOR specs, same CCA/HDPE/AL-foil+Mylar/AL-MG/PVC construction), which look like later re-namings of the same 300M rolls; they are not named in any thread carrying this file, so I left them out. sources.subject: Cat.5e patch cord ROHS2.0
sources.evidence:
DOCUMENT IDENTITY PROVEN (not a catalogue guess). I rendered the image itself at /Users/lanstar/mail2/제품인증자료/_미확정/Cat.5e patch cord_RoHS_CatchFC24.jpg: it reads "4. Cat6/6A/7/8  S/FTP（PIMF）, Copper, CCA-PVC,LSZH / Sample No.: WTH20H05025692C01 / Sample Received Date: May 11, 2020 / Testing Period: May 11, 2020 - May 15, 2020 / Test Requested: ... EU RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU and its amendment Directive EU 2015/863 / PASS", with hand-added red "RoHS" and "RoHS 2.0" callouts (Gu's annotations illustrating his 2023-03-23 argument). I then extracted page 1 of /Users/lanstar/mail2/제품인증자료/문서/LS-8SSTP-200MG_RoHS_搏莱 WTH20H05025692X1C-1 -ROHS.pdf (shasum confirms d2f674d62662d815106b5182a582d13048259f59, 16 pages): identical text, including the full-width parentheses in "S/FTP（PIMF）". The JPG is a crop of page 1 of report WTH20H05025692X1C-1 (HCT, CNAS L4136, dated 2020-05-19). manifest.jsonl contains exactly one document with root WTH20H05025692, so there is no ambiguity.

ORIGINAL REJECTION REASON WAS A CROP ARTIFACT. The visible "4. Cat6/6A/7/8 S/FTP(PIMF)" is the LAST of four Client's Ref lines; the PDF shows the full Sample Name block: "1. U/UTP Patch Cord Cable / 2. F/UTP Patch Cord Cable / 3. SF/UTP Patch Cord Cable / 4. S/FTP (PIMF) Patch Cord Cable". Sample 1 is precisely the Cat.5e U/UTP patch cord kyu requested ("We need Cat.5e patch cord ROHS sheet", 2023-03-23). The prior note that the screenshot shows "a Cat6/6A/7/8 S/FTP cable, not the Cat.5e patch cord" is refuted. Product type therefore matches: RJ45-terminated network patch cord, all four shielding constructions, Applicant Ningbo Borland Electronic Co., Ltd. — the same BOR factory that supplies these Lanstar series.

CITED EVIDENCE VERIFIED. manifest.jsonl line 252 for doc_id d2f674d62662 carries verbatim the quoted source: {"mail_key":"INBOX:9922","subject":"patch cord ROHS2.0","date":"2023-03-23","evidence":"GU 2023-03-23 body explicitly lists these ten patch cord series (Borland own factory) as covered by this RoHS 2.0 sheet","confidence":"high"}. Minor imprecision in the claim: that is a same-day SIBLING thread ("patch cord ROHS2.0", INBOX:9922), not literally this packet's thread ("Cat.5e patch cord ROHS2.0"). Does not affect the linkage. The manifest also records four further supplier-attested sources: INBOX:11493 (2023-07-25/27, Gu names LS-8SSTP-200MG and attaches this ROHS sheet), INBOX:14389 (2024-03-27, kyu lists LS-5UTP-100MG / LS-5UTP-100MBL, Gu replies with this file), INBOX:11882 (2023-08-30, TPE high-flex cord = LS-HF7xx), INBOX:8197 (2022-09-22, CAT.5e FTP 300M BOR-2207001 = LS-CAT.5E-FTP-300M).

WHY REVISE — the models list is wrong in form. The claim submitted 14 FAMILY STEMS as models. Checked against the archive registry (byModel, 715 entries, parsed out of 제품인증자료_보고서.html): LSP-7UTP, LS-8SFTP, LS-F6-UTPD, LS-F6UTPD, LS-F7-UTPD, LS-5UTP and LS-CAT.5E-FTP are NOT registered model codes at all, and LS-5UTPD is a registered model DISTINCT from LS-5UTPD-XXM. A chatbot querying LS-5UTP-100MG or LS-6UTPD-XXM would fail to match the claim's list. The identical full report is physically filed in 15 model folders under 제품인증자료/모델별/ and manifest.jsonl assigns it exactly those 15 model codes — which I have substituted. FAMILIES ARE CORRECT AS CLAIMED: the manifest's families array is exactly the same 14 (verified set-equal), so the 14-family catalogue grep, though partly an artifact of family_catalog_short.json truncating every entry to 260 chars (362 of 364 entries hit the cap), is independently corroborated by the authoritative manifest.

NO ALTERNATIVE FAMILY FITS. This is not a generic "same product category" inference — the model set is inherited from a byte-identical parent report, so no competing family can be substituted.

CAVEAT TO CARRY FORWARD (from the archive's own caveat_ko on d2f674d62662): the tested samples are RJ45-assembled patch cords; the drum/bulk cable models LS-8SSTP-200MG, LS-CAT.5E-FTP-300M and LS-5UTP-100MG/100MBL are NOT in the sample list. Those four links rest on supplier attestation (the mails above) and a "same raw material, same factory" rationale, which must be stated when serving this document for a drum-cable RoHS request. Also: the applicant is Ningbo Borland, no Lanstar model code appears anywhere in the document, it is a 2020 issue, and this JPG is only a cropped page 1 — the full 16-page PDF (d2f674d6…) should be sent instead of the screenshot whenever an actual certificate is requested. [검증-수정]

sources.subject: Re: Cat.5e UTP patch cord CE certification
sources.evidence:
SUBSTANCE CONFIRMED; revision is only to the model-code strings (families unchanged from the claim).

1) Cited evidence all verifies. shasum shows 제품인증자료/_미확정/"Cat.5e UTP patch cord (network patch cor_CE_网络跳线-EMC报告.pdf" and 제품인증자료/문서/LS-6SFTP-300M_TestReport_网络跳线-EMC报告.pdf are both deafdce6433cee08e9fabb0d662b62a07124e907 (byte-identical). manifest.jsonl line 108 records exactly the claimed 6 models / 6 families with the five request-mail sources quoted (INBOX:4102 2021-04-20 names LS-6SFTP-300M; INBOX:6051 2021-12-08 names LS-SSTP-CAT.6A-300M; INBOX:6737 2022-03-15 "cable is same as F/UTP Cat.5e patch cord LS-5STPD-xxMG so patch-cord CE applies to LS-FTP-300MSTG"; INBOX:20721 2025-06-16 LS-HF series; INBOX:14003 2024-02-21 cat.7 patch cord -> LS-7SSTPD-XMG). family_catalog.json carries report BCTC-FY190200494E under LS-6SFTP-300M, LS-FTP, LS-HF SERIES and the paired certificate BCTC-FY190200494C under LS-SSTP-CAT6A-300M, as claimed.

2) Product type genuinely matches. The report's own Model Number block declares "NPC-ABC-D-E ... A: 5E, 6, 6A, 7, 8 (Category); B: 1 to 6 (Structure, 1: U/UTP ...)" — Cat.5e U/UTP patch cord is inside the tested series declaration, not an inference. Manufacturer is Ningbo Borland / applicant Xiangshan Bor, and LS-5UTPD's two datasheets in the archive are BOR drawings for the same manufacturer. In this thread (2021-12-20) kyu asks Gu for "CE certification for Cat.5e UTP patch cord" and Gu answers with precisely this file plus the CE certificate and the RoHS pair, adding "actually I sent them to you before" — the supplier himself asserts applicability to Cat.5e UTP patch cord.

3) Refutation attempts failed. Alternative Cat.5e families were checked one by one: LS-5UTP (LS-5UTP-100MBL/100MG), LS-UTP5H (= LS-CAT.5E-HUTP-300M, 300m drum) and LS-CAT.5E-HUTP are bulk cable, not patch cords; LS-CAT5E-UTP is a bare RJ45 plug family (its docs are connector/plating/brass RoHS); LS-5STPD, LS-5STPC, LS-5FTPSD-BK, LS-CAT.5E-FTP are shielded (F/UTP), not UTP. The only genuine rival is LS-5UTPAD (angled Cat.5e U/UTP patch cord), but it is a niche variant and already carries the equivalent BCTC2511748719E/C CE-EMC pair, whereas LS-5UTPD — 14 length/colour model codes 0.5M~50M, 18 docs — currently has NO CE/EMC document at all, which is exactly the gap this 2021-12-20 request was filling. LS-5UTPD is therefore specific, not a generic catalogue guess. (If the pipeline wants maximal coverage, LS-5UTPAD-*M could be added later, but it is not needed and I did not add it.)

4) The defect: the claim set models = families, which yields strings that are not real model codes. 모델조회표.csv has no bare "LS-FTP" or "LS-7SSTPD" entries; the archive's canonical codes for this document are LS-FTP-300MSTG, LS-7SSTPD-XMG, LS-5STPD-XXMG (LS-6SFTP-300M, LS-SSTP-CAT.6A-300M and LS-HF SERIES are already correct as-is). For the new family the registered wildcard code is LS-5UTPD-XXM (the same form used by the sibling HCT RoHS report). Families list is accepted verbatim from the claim.

Caveat to carry forward (already in the manifest record): this is the 22-page EMC test report, not the CE certificate — pair it with BCTC-FY190200494C (sha1 4090bb7e…) when a customer asks for "the CE certificate", and note that the Lanstar model codes do not appear in the document itself. sources.subject: Re: Cat.5e UTP patch cord CE certification
sources.evidence: EVIDENCE CHECKS OUT: retry_packets/r_001.json carries the full 2021-12-20 thread — kyu asks Mr Gu (guzhiyi@bor-cable.com) for "CE certification for Cat.5e UTP patch cord"; Gu replies with exactly the four attachments 网络跳线-EMC报告/证书 + -ROHS报告/证书, of which this sha1 is 网络跳线-EMC证书.pdf. Cert scope confirmed: NPC-ABC-D-E, A=5E/6/6A/7/8, B=1~6 (U/UTP…S/FTP), C=01~99 mould, D=0010~5000 length, E=colour; Applicant Xiangshan Bor / Manufacturer Ningbo Borland (=BOR, the thread's supplier). So a Cat.5e U/UTP cord is squarely inside the declared scope. PRODUCT TYPE MATCH IS EXACT AND THE FAMILY IS UNIQUE: family_catalog.json (note the _short file is truncated at 260 chars; the full family_catalog.json confirms the quoted text) plus final_data.json show LS-5UTPD = "CAT.5E U/UTP 다이렉트(스트레이트 T568B) 패치코드, 양단 CAT.5E RJ45 언실드 플러그, CCA, BOR 사양서 2020-09-14", supported by TWO BOR drawings (33cf20f2 LS-5UTPD-xxMx SOLID.pdf = 0.5M/1M 24AWG solid; 5d13e49f LS-5UTPD-xxMx.pdf = 2M~50M 26AWG stranded) and 13 Fluke DSX-8000 channel reports LS-5UTPD-0.5MG…-50MG. No rival family fits: LS-5STPC is F/UTP shielded CROSS, LS-5STPD is F/UTP straight, LS-5UTP is a 100 m bulk cable (members LS-5UTP-100MG/100MBL), LS-UTP5H is 300 m bulk, LS-CAT.5E-HUTP/-SFTP/-FTP are bulk cable. Category+shielding+construction+connector+form factor all agree. WHY REVISE — TWO DEFECTS IN THE CLAIM: (1) Model codes are wrong-form and arbitrarily truncated. "MX" is the colour placeholder used on the drawing, not a real Lanstar code — across the whole archive LS-5UTPD-0.5MG occurs 93x and LS-5UTPD-1MG 42x, while LS-5UTPD-0.5MX/-1MX occur only 4x each (only inside that one drawing). members_of in final_data.json lists LS-5UTPD-0.5MG,1MG,2MG,2MB,3MG,5MG,7MG,10MG,15MG,20MG,30MG,50MG. Restricting to 0.5M/1M comes from reading only the SOLID drawing; the sibling drawing covers 2M–50M and the certificate's own D field (0010–5000 mm = 0.1–50 m) covers the entire family, so all 12 length/colour codes are covered. (2) The 19-family list is over-broad and internally incoherent. NPC-ABC-D-E has NO round/flat/slim dimension, so the flat families (LS-F6-UTPD, LS-F7-UTPD, LS-F7FTP, LS-F8FTP, LS-FT6U) and the 32AWG slim families (LS-SL6, LS-6AUTP, LS-6AFTP) are not inside the declared scope — the later BOR cert BCTC2511421501CN1 (2026) explicitly adds "ROUND/FLAT/SLIM" to its scope line, which shows the 2019 cert did not carry it. The list also contains alias duplicates (LS-6UTPD ≡ LS-CAT.6-UTPD; LS-6UTPC ≡ LS-CAT.6-UTPC) and, if it were meant as a full-scope list, it inconsistently omits LS-5STPD, LS-FTP, LS-6SFTP-300M, LS-SSTP-CAT6A-300M, LS-7SSTPD and LS-HF SERIES, which are ALREADY attached to this same sha1 from five other threads (see final_data.json docs entry). The list appears copied from a different document's spread (HCT RoHS report d2f674d6, whose scope is genuinely broader). The thread evidence supports exactly one new link: the Cat.5e U/UTP patch cord family LS-5UTPD, which currently has no CE in the coverage matrix (batch_notes.json: LS-5UTPD CE="X"), so this fills a real gap. RESIDUAL DOUBT: LS-5UTPAD-*M is a separate Cat.5e patch-cord code kyu uses in 2026 mails (listed alongside LS-6UTPD-*M/6UTPC-*M/6STPD-*M) and already carries the 2026 BOR CE; it has no data sheet in the archive so I could not determine whether it is a distinct product or a later naming of the same cord. It does not refute LS-5UTPD for a 2021 thread, but a human should reconcile the two codes. [검증-수정] | 동일 파일이 다른 메일에서 이미 확정됨(중복 병합)

sources.subject: Re: Cat.5e UTP patch cord CE certification
sources.evidence:
Evidence cited is real: r_001.json doc[1]; thread Sent:2137 -> INBOX:6152 (2021-12-20), kyu asks CE for "Cat.5e UTP patch cord", Gu attaches EMC+RoHS report/cert; no Lanstar code in thread or doc (applicant Xiangshan Bor, model NPC-6A601-0200-GY).

CORE LINK HOLDS (and is stronger than a bare catalogue match): the report's own declared scope NPC-ABC-D-E has A=5E and B=1 (U/UTP), i.e. it literally enumerates the requested product. LS-5UTPD is the only Cat.5e U/UTP PATCH CORD family among the 364 catalogue keys (LS-5UTP = 100M/305M bulk roll, LS-UTP5H = 300M roll, LS-5STPC/LS-5STPD = F/UTP, LS-5UTPAD-*M appears only in 2026 mails with its own 2025/26 BCTC docs). Same manufacturer (BOR drawing text names "BOR INTERNATIONAL TRADE CO.,LTD"), and construction matches the tested parts: LS-5UTPD is 4*2*1/0.50CCA + PVC jacket, grey (-xMG); the report tested PVC wire jackets in 12 colours incl. Gray. final_data.json matrix shows LS-5UTPD with RoHS=X, CE=X, a genuine gap.

REVISION 1 - models too narrow. "LS-5UTPD-0.5MX/-1MX" is the model list of only the SOLID 24AWG drawing (doc_text sha1 33cf20f2...). The stranded drawing (5d13e49f...) lists -2MX..-20MX and the BOR quotation U-UTP CAT.5E PATCH CORD-50M.xlsx lists LS-5UTPD-0.5MG..-50MG; members_of already holds LS-5UTPD-XXM / -XMG. As claimed, a chatbot would serve this RoHS report only for 0.5m and 1m cords. "X" is also a colour placeholder (*X=G/R), not an orderable suffix.

REVISION 2 - the 19-family blanket is refuted. BOR itself certifies slim and flat cords separately: on 2026-07-08 Gu sent the general "Network cable" RoHS/CE in INBOX:27455 and then a SEPARATE mail INBOX:27456 "for slim patch cord and flat patch" with distinct reports (BCTC2511173018E "Network slim patch cord"). The 2019 NPC-ABC-D-E code has axes only for Category/Structure/Mould/Length/Colour - no form-factor axis - while the later 2025 BCTC report explicitly enumerates ROUND/FLAT/SLIM. So LS-SL6, LS-6AUTP, LS-6AFTP (32AWG slim LSZH) and LS-F6-UTPD, LS-F7-UTPD, LS-F7FTP, LS-F8FTP (flat) are outside its scope. LS-F8FTP (drawing 2025-07-04) and LS-7NSTPD (2025-04-27, LSZH+nylon braid) post-date the 2019 report and use jackets it never tested. sources.subject: Re: Cat.5e UTP patch cord CE certification
sources.evidence:
CORE IDENTIFICATION SURVIVES; THE MODEL LIST AND THE FAMILY FAN-OUT DO NOT.

1) Cited evidence is real. retry_packets/r_001.json, doc 32560fab (网络跳线-ROHS证书.pdf), thread = 2 messages of 2021-12-20: kyu "Our customer want receive about CE certification for Cat.5e UTP patch cord", Gu replies with 4 attachments incl. this file. final_data.json/unresolved confirms it is mail INBOX:6152.

2) Product type genuinely matches. product_in_doc = "NETWORK PATCH CORD / NPC-ABC-D-E (A=5E,6,6A,7,8 / B=1~6 U/UTP~S/FTP / C=mold / D=length 0010~5000 / E=colour)". A=5E, B=1 is exactly a Cat.5e U/UTP patch cord. Finished-product scope. No category/shielding/connector mismatch.

3) LS-5UTPD is the unique catalogue match, and independently corroborated (not just by the drawing the claim quotes): 12 Fluke reports in final_data.json are titled "LS-5UTPD-xMG Cat.5e U/UTP 다이렉트 패치코드". Competitors all fail on a spec axis: LS-5STPC = F/UTP cross, LS-5STPD = F/UTP direct, LS-5UTP = 100 m bulk drum cable, LS-UTP5H / LS-CAT.5E-HUTP / LS-C5U305* = 300–305 m bulk cable, LS-CAT.5E-FTP = bulk F/UTP. Only residual ambiguity is the ERP code LS-5UTPAD-*M, whose product type is never described in the archive and which first appears 2026-07-08, 4.5 years after this thread — not a real competitor for 2021.

4) DEFECT A — the model codes do not exist. Of 715 distinct model codes in final_data.json, ZERO end in "MX"; there is no LS-5UTPD-0.5MX or LS-5UTPD-1MX. The real codes are LS-5UTPD-0.5MG … -50MG (G = grey; the trailing X in the drawing is a colour placeholder). The resolver's own convention for these drawings is LS-5UTPD-XMG / LS-5UTPD-XXM (see doc 5d13e49f, 33cf20f2, d2f674d6).

5) DEFECT B — the 0.5 m/1 m restriction is an artifact. "LS-5UTPD-0.5MX, LS-5UTPD-1MX" is the model list of ONE drawing, LS-5UTPD-xxMx SOLID.pdf (sha1 33cf20f2), the 24AWG SOLID variant. The sibling drawing LS-5UTPD-xxMx.pdf (5d13e49f) covers 2M/3M/5M/7M/10M/15M/20M/30M/50M in 26AWG STRANDED. The 2021-12-20 mail names no length, and the certificate's own length field is 0010~5000 (0.1–50 m), so restricting to the two solid short cords excludes the mainstream models a customer would actually ask about.

6) DEFECT C — the 19-family fan-out is unsupported and inconsistent. This sha1 is already resolved in final_data.json against 9 models via 8 other mails (LS-6SFTP-300M, LS-7SSTPD-XMG, LS-SSTP-CAT.6A-300M, LS-UTP5H-300MG, LS-7UTP-300MG, LS-FTP-300MSTG, LS-5STPD-XXMG, LS-HF SERIES, LS-F7-SFTP-XM). The claim's list contains NONE of those — including LS-5STPD, which is squarely in the certificate scope and already accepted for this same file — while adding families the 2021-12-20 mail never touches. It also lists LS-5STPC among the families after arguing in its own rationale that LS-5STPC does not match "UTP".

7) DEFECT D — several claimed families sit outside the certificate's stated designator. NPC-ABC-D-E has no form-factor or jacket-material dimension, and the tested sample was NPC-6A601-0200-GY, a round Cat.6A S/FTP 2 m cord. The claim nevertheless sweeps in slim and flat cords: LS-SL6 (slim 32AWG LSZH OD 2.8 mm), LS-6AUTP / LS-6AFTP (slim Cat.6A 32AWG), LS-F7FTP (32AWG flat Cat.6A U/FTP), LS-F8FTP (flat U/FTP Cat.8), LS-FT6U (transparent). It is BOR's LATER certificate BCTC2511421501CN1 (2026-01-29) that explicitly adds "ROUND/FLAT/SLIM" and TPE/PUR/NYLON jackets — the 2019 one does not. Worse, the archive's RoHS evidence for the slim Cat.6A cords (LS-6AUTP/LS-6AFTP, "PATCH CORD ROHS.pdf") is a Bureau Veritas report for 浙江一舟 production, a different manufacturer from the Ningbo Borland named on this certificate. Sending this cert for those models is exactly the wrong-product hand-off the review is meant to prevent.

REVISED LINK: this mail occurrence resolves to family LS-5UTPD, all lengths (models above). Note for the pipeline: this is an additional source for a document that already has independent coverage from 8 other mails — the LS-5UTPD attachment should be added to that coverage, not replace it. sources.subject: Re: Cat.6 UTP 300m cable.
sources.evidence:
EVIDENCE VERIFIED. r_025.json holds the full 13-message thread "Cat.6 UTP 300m cable." (2021-07-09 .. 2021-07-13). Msg 0 (kyu, 2021-07-09): "Could you please check the Resistance (ohms) about CAT.6 UTP 300M cable? ... our customer want fluke test report." Msg 1 (guzhiyi@bor-cable.com, 2021-07-12): "We just tested your U/UTP Cat.6 Lan Cable-BLUE color by 80m and 70m and 60m ... 3) 80m failed", attaching exactly "CAT6 UTP 60M/70M/80M 24AWG.pdf" — this sha1 is the 80M one. Msg 3: "must use copper conductor cable, not CCA conductor cable"; msg 12 prices it as "28% copper CCA". PDF internals match: Cable ID CAT6 UTP 80M, Cable Type Cat 6 U/UTP, 255 ft, operator BLOQC, 2021-07-12 13:12, FAIL on RL. So the document is BOR's own test of the Lanstar-supplied Cat.6 U/UTP 24AWG CCA bulk cable off a 300 m reel, blue jacket. Cited evidence is accurate, nothing overstated.

PRODUCT TYPE IS GENUINELY THE SAME. Category (Cat.6), shielding (U/UTP unshielded), construction (4P 24AWG CCA solid), form factor (300 m bulk box, not a patch cord), colour (blue) all line up with catalogue family LS-6UTP: "U/UTP CAT.6 CABLE / MODEL: LS-6UTP-300 series / CUSTOMER: LANstar ... 실내용 U/UTP CAT.6 랜케이블 4P 24AWG CCA 300m ... 자켓색 Grey 또는 Blue".

NO RIVAL FAMILY FITS. LS-CAT.6-SFTP-300M is double-shielded (report says U/UTP); LS-C6OD300 is outdoor PE black (tested reel is blue PVC indoor); LS-CAT.5E-HUTP / LS-UTP5H-300MG — the only LS code appearing in the thread — is Cat.5e and is used only in a "like LS-UTP5H-300MG" copper-content comparison for a NEW purple order, so the first pass was right to distrust it; LS-CAT.6-UTPD/UTPC/SL6/FT6U are stranded patch cords. LS-6UTP is the sole indoor Cat.6 U/UTP 300 m bulk family. Independent corroboration: kyu's 2021-06-28 mail (two weeks before this test) "Rohs2.0 for CAT.6 UTP cable." names LS-6UTP-300MG, and the archive holds Fluke reports whose Cable IDs are literally LS-6UTP-300MG / -300MBK / -300MP / -300MR / -300MY.

WHY REVISE RATHER THAN CONFIRM. The family is right; the model string is not a real SKU. "LS-6UTP-300" occurs nowhere in the archive as a code — it is only the prose phrase "LS-6UTP-300 series" in the spec title (grep for '"LS-6UTP-300"' in final_data.json and family_catalog.json returns 0). BOR's model-mapping spreadsheet (attachments_raw/INBOX_13651/lan cable (1).xlsx, thread "Re: New order", 2024-01-08) gives the canonical rename: old "LS-CAT.6-UTP-300M" -> new "LS-6UTP-300M", description "U/UTP Cat.6 Lan Cable, 4*2*1/0.50CCA(8% Copper), PVC, 300m/Box". The same sheet (INBOX_13491 version) lists the colour SKUs: "LS-6UTP-300MG ... PVC, Grey" and "LS-6UTP-300MB ... PVC, Blue" (both $23.62). Since Gu explicitly tested the BLUE reel, the precise SKU is LS-6UTP-300MB, under the series code LS-6UTP-300M. Grey (LS-6UTP-300MG) is deliberately excluded — same construction but not the reel tested.

CAVEAT FOR THE CHATBOT: this is a FAIL report (ISO11801 Class E, RL fail at 80 m) on the 8%-copper CCA product, produced as a diagnostic, not a conformity certificate. It should never be served as "the Fluke pass certificate" for LS-6UTP. The pass reports in the archive are the 2024-09-10 set (LS-6UTP-300MBK/MP/MR/MY) and the LS-6UTP-300MG report. Note also that the purple 28-30%-copper cable kyu orders at the end of this thread is a different, higher-copper build that later appears as LS-6UTP-300MP. [검증-수정]

sources.subject: Re: Cat.6 UTP 300m cable.
sources.evidence:
FAMILY CONFIRMED, MODEL CODE REFINED. All cited evidence checks out verbatim in /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/retry_packets/r_025.json (doc index 0; PDF at .../attachments_raw/INBOX_4780/CAT6 UTP 60M 24AWG.pdf). Msg 0 (2021-07-09, kyu->guzhiyi@bor-cable.com, subj "Cat.6 UTP 300m cable."): "Could you please check the Resistance (ohms) about CAT.6 UTP 300M cable?". Msg 1 (2021-07-12, Gu, attaches CAT6 UTP 60M/70M/80M 24AWG.pdf): "We just tested your U/UTP Cat.6 Lan Cable-BLUE color by 80m and 70m and 60m this morning!... 1) 60m pass testing easily." Msg 3: "must use copper conductor cable, not CCA conductor cable" and msg 12: "it's 28% copper CCA" — so the tested roll is the existing low-copper CCA item, not solid BC. Product type matches on every axis: Cat.6, U/UTP (unshielded), CCA solid 24AWG, 300 m bulk box, indoor PVC — the report's own header reads Cable Type "Cat 6 U/UTP", and measured loop resistance 17.67 ohm / 196 ft = ~29.6 ohm/100m, i.e. ~1.6x solid copper, consistent with 8% CCA, not BC.

WHY THE MODEL STRING NEEDS REVISING: "LS-6UTP-300" is not an item code that exists anywhere in the archive; the family is colour-suffixed. BOR's own quotation attachment (.../attachments_raw/INBOX_13491/lan cable.xlsx, columns "Item no. | New Item No. | Description | Package | Unit Price") reads: old item LS-CAT.6-UTP-300M -> new items LS-6UTP-300MG = "U/UTP Cat.6 Lan Cable, 4*2*1/0.50CCA(8% Copper), PVC, Grey, 300m/Box, 23.62" and LS-6UTP-300MB = same line but "...PVC, Blue, 300m/Box, 23.62". The label sheet .../attachments_raw/INBOX_18232/LAN cable-LABEL DETAIL.xlsx repeats the same mapping and shows the full colour set LS-6UTP-300MG/MB/MBK/MR/MY/MP (grey/blue/black/red/yellow/purple). Gu tested the BLUE cable, so the item is LS-6UTP-300MB. The code predates the test: a Sent mail 2020-12-22 to Mr Gu has subject exactly "LS-6UTP-300MB" (survey.json, Sent uid 1000), and kyu named LS-6UTP-300MG in a RoHS request only 11 days before the test (2021-06-28, "Rohs2.0 for CAT.6 UTP cable.", kb_docs sha 3364d755/0fbf4292). So the 2024-01-18 LS-6UTP-300 datasheet is not an anachronism — the family was live in 2021.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED (no other family fits): LS-CAT.6-SFTP-300M / LS-6SFTP-300M are SF/UTP double-shielded; LS-C6OD300 is outdoor PE black; LS-6FTP-100MG / LS-CAT.6-FTP-300M are F/UTP; LS-CAT.6-UTPD / LS-6UTPC / LS-6UTPD are stranded patch cords with RJ45 moulds, not bulk; LS-SSTP-CAT.6A-300M is Cat.6A S/FTP; LS-6UTP-100MG is a 100 m box and grey only. In the whole 364-family catalogue and both BOR item sheets, the only Cat.6 U/UTP CCA 300 m box in BLUE is LS-6UTP-300MB. The earlier pass's rejected candidate LS-UTP5H-300MG is correctly refuted: it is the Cat.5e 28%-CCA grey item (lan cable.xlsx: "U/UTP Cat.5e Lan Cable, 4*2*1/0.50CCA(28% Copper), PVC, Grey"), and kyu only cites it in msg 7 as a copper-content benchmark for a NEW purple order. Sibling reports ee2fe7d7 (70M) and d1ef5f08 (80M, FAIL) from the same 2021-07-12 mail belong to the same item and should be revised the same way. [검증-수정]

sources.subject: Re: Re: COC or CE sheet for cat.7 patch cord
sources.evidence: Thread request (Sent 2024-02-21): kyu — 'We need COC or CE sheet for cat.7 SSTP patch cord.' Supplier answer in the same thread (2024-02-28): Gu — 'As for the S/FTP Cat.6A/7 patch cords, Ship company have ETL and EC certificate, please find attached file', attaching this EC statement plus the ETL certificate; kyu closes with 'Thank you so much'. The thread names no Lanstar code, but the Lanstar model behind kyu's phrase 'cat.7 (S)STP patch cord' is fixed elsewhere with the same correspondent: Sent:2968 (2022-10-12) 'CMRT for cat.7 patch cords ... about LS-7SSTPD-xMG'; Sent:4624 (2024-04-24, two months after this thread) 'CAT.7 patch cords(LS-7SSTPD-xM)'; INBOX:14698 (2024-04-24) Gu — 'LS-7SSTPD-xM series of patch cords are made by Ship company'; INBOX:9805 (2023-03-13) Gu — 'the ROHS sheet can use below patch cords: LS-7SSTPD-xxMG, LS-F7-SFTP-xxM, LS-SL6-xxB, LS-SL6-xxW, LS-6AUTP-xxM, LS-6AFTP-xxM. Because above patch cords are from Ship company!', and in the preceding message 'S/FTP Cat.7 patch cords produce by Ship company'. Independent confirmation from the attachments themselves: the Fluke DTX-1800 reports for LS-7SSTPD-0.5MG…-50MG (INBOX:5699, 2021-10-29, sent in answer to kyu's request for the LS-7SSTPD-10M report) carry 'Cable Type: Cat 7 S/FTP' and 'Operator: SHIPQC' — Ship's own QC lab — and the BOR order sheet describes 'LS-7SSTPD-10MG, S/FTP Cat.7 Patch Cord, 26AWG, LSZH, Grey, 10m'. So the Ship S/FTP Cat.6A/7 patch cord that this EC channel statement covers is Lanstar family LS-7SSTPD (length/colour variants LS-7SSTPD-0.5MG … -50MG). [검증완료]

sources.subject: Customs sheet to export
sources.evidence:
The claim's quoted facts are real, but its conclusion inverts the evidence. It drops the ONE family the archive actually ties this file to and substitutes 12 families that appear nowhere near it.

WHAT CHECKS OUT
- Report identity verified in /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/reach_full.txt (19 pages, full text): BV Lab No. (2420)104-0118, 2020-04-23, Applicant "NINGBO EOXUN NETWORKING CO.,LTD", Manufacturer / Style No. / PO No. all blank ("/"), sample = "U/UTP、F/UTP、SF/UTP、S/FTP---PVC、LSZH--- CAT5E、CAT6、CAT6A、CAT3---ROUND &FLAT PATCH CORD", tested as Soft-plastic group 1+2 and Metal group. No CAT7 and no model code anywhere. So it is genuinely a line-level, model-less REACH report — the claim is right about that.
- Thread (INBOX:4183, r_005.json) is as described: kyu 2021-04-27 asks export data for "cat.7 patch code to Poland (LS-7SSTPD-Xm)"; Gu 2021-04-30 replies "compliant with RoHS and Reach is enough" and attaches this file.

WHY THE 12-FAMILY LIST IS WRONG
1. No evidentiary link at all. This sha1 appears in exactly two mails, both LS-7SSTPD requests, both from guzhiyi@bor-cable.com. Not one Cat.5e/Cat.6 model is named in either. The 12 families are pure type-similarity guessing.
2. The set is arbitrary / non-unique — the claim's own stated test fails. The report's scope also covers CAT6A, CAT3, S/FTP and FLAT, so these catalogue families fit the scope line exactly as well and are omitted with no stated reason: LS-6AUTP (Cat.6A U/UTP), LS-HF701/702/703/705/707/710/715/720/730/750 and LS-HF SERIES (Cat.6A S/FTP), LS-SL6 / LS-SL6-XXX / LS-SL6-XXB / LS-SL6-XXW (slim Cat.6 U/UTP), LS-FT6U / LS-FT6UXXM (Cat.6 U/UTP FLAT — while the claim does include flat Cat.6 LS-F6UTPD), LS-6SFTP-300M, LS-FTP, LS-UTP5H, LS-5UTPAD, LS-BFTP7. A different family fits equally well, so the match is too weak.
3. Wrong applicant. Ningbo Eoxun is not Lanstar's supplier (Xiangshan Bor / Ningbo Borland) and appears nowhere else in this archive. Attaching a third party's report to LS-6UTPD/LS-5UTPD etc. on shape alone is exactly the "wrong product's certificate" failure this review guards against. The report also self-disclaims: results "are not indicative or representative of ... any similar or identical product unless specifically and expressly noted."

THE CORRECT LINK: LS-7SSTPD
- kb_docs.json['docs'] already carries this exact sha1 with models ["LS-7SSTPD-XM"], stored as "LS-7SSTPD-XM_REACH_PATCH CORD REACH 2021-04-23.pdf", marked "verified":"revise" from an earlier sweep. aggregated.json['rows'] for INBOX:4183 likewise has model "LS-7SSTPD-XM".
- Byte-identical file (shasum confirmed) sits in attachments_raw/INBOX_3980/ and attachments_raw/INBOX_4183/. INBOX:3980 (2021-04-02, subject "CAT.7 SSTP / Reach or MSDS sheet") is the supplier's direct answer to kyu's "We need REACH or MSDS sheet for cat.7 sstp patch cords", where Gu writes verbatim: "S/FTP Cat.6A/7 patch cords are from Ship company! Please find attached Reach test report! By the way, actually the rest [test] report is suitable for all of your patch cords!"
- Third confirmation: INBOX:23029 (2025, "Request for Compliance Certificates – LS-7SSTPD-xM Patch Cord") supplies the successor report "PATCH CORD REACH.pdf" (sha1 b1b6304a…, BV (6625)073-0550, 2025-03-26) for the same model — same generic patch-cord scope, same purpose.
- LS-7SSTPD is a valid catalogue family (family_catalog.json), and this report is already its first catalogue entry.

Note on the claim's one good argument: the tested scope does stop at CAT6A, so this report does not literally test a Cat.7 cord. That is a delivery caveat (already recorded in enrichment.json's caveat_ko), not a reason to reassign the document to a dozen unrelated families. models=[] because the mails write the length as a placeholder ("LS-7SSTPD-Xm"); the archive's stored string is "LS-7SSTPD-XM". If a broad line-level fan-out is later wanted, LS-7SSTPD must be in the set and the Cat.6A/slim/flat families above must be included too. [검증-수정] | 동일 파일이 다른 메일에서 이미 확정됨(중복 병합)

As for LS-1800HBS, it is from Jiasheng company' — the attachments being LS-800HQ-1200HQ.pdf, LS-1600HQ-2000HQ.pdf and LS-1600HSQ-2000HSQ.pdf, i.e. exactly the HQ (601S) and HSQ (VE) 19-inch rack cabinet series. Those nine models are the Lanstar 19" cabinets built by Zhejiang Ship, and they are all present as families in the Lanstar catalogue (601S / VE series, 19" server-rack cabinets). Counter-evidence for the other cabinets: INBOX:17825 (2024-12-02) has Gu listing LS-300H, LS-500H, LS-750H, LS-1000H, LS-1200H, LS-1600H, LS-1800H, LS-2000H and LS-750HS~LS-2000HS as Jiasheng cabinets, so those are covered by the Jiasheng CE set, not by this one. [검증완료]

sources.subject: Re: Inquiry About CoC Sheet for LS-CON44 RJ11 Connector
sources.evidence:
The cited 2026-05-14 mail is real (retry_packets/r_010.json, doc index 2; Gu answers kyu's LS-CON44 RJ11 CoC request with 'CE certificate for all RJ45 connectors', attaching UTP/FTP RJ45-CE证书.pdf). But the catalogue-guess method was unnecessary and wrong: this identical file (same sha1, same 346903 bytes) was ALSO sent earlier by the same supplier, and that instance is already resolved by direct mail evidence.

Direct evidence — /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lanstar-mail2/752f8fc5-be77-4ab5-bb66-347588e328d1/scratchpad/bodies.json:
• Sent:4710, kyu 2024-05-14, subject 'CE certificate for RJ45 connector': "If you have CE certificate for RJ45 connector, Please send it. LS-CAT5E-UTP / CAT6-UTP / CAT6-STP..."
• INBOX:14974, Gu 2024-05-16: "Please find attached CE certificate for UTP and FTP RJ45 connectors", attachments 'UTP RJ45 connector-CE证书.pdf' sha1=bc1de4b9a151da1330bf1966eadc4b04a57a4f7b and 'FTP RJ45 connector-CE证书.pdf' sha1=104f9140e8ea61323edfd9dd31d203ac1cc1c1a4.
The UTP attestation ('Unshielded crystal head / Part No.: UTP PLUG') therefore maps to the two unshielded connector models kyu named — LS-CAT5E-UTP and LS-CAT6-UTP — while its FTP sibling maps to LS-CAT6-STP. final_data.json already records exactly this ('models': ['LS-CAT5E-UTP','LS-CAT6-UTP'], confidence high); only the 2026 re-send instance (INBOX:26438) was left unresolved because it fails to cover the RJ11 item kyu actually asked about.

Corroboration that these are live Lanstar model codes for BOR RJ45 plugs, not kyu shorthand: Sent:4113 (2023-12-04) 'We need RJ45 connector ROHS sheet. CAT5E-UTP / STP, CAT6-UTP / STP'; Sent:3385 (2023-03-03) requests RoHS for LS-CAT5E-UTP, answered with Wenzhou Yihua plug material RoHS reports (gold layer, tin layer, H62/H65 brass, PC L-1250Y) which final_data links to LS-CAT5E-UTP; the codes also recur throughout BOR order threads. final_data['family_of'] resolves LS-CAT5E-UTP and LS-CAT6-UTP each to their own family.

Why the proposed LS-C5K / LS-PASS-7UTP link fails: (a) it is a pure catalogue guess with zero mail evidence, and the proposer's own note concedes two families 'fit equally well' — in fact at least four unshielded RJ45-plug families fit (LS-C5K, LS-PASS-7UTP, LS-CAT5E-UTP, LS-CAT6-UTP), the latter two invisible in family_catalog_short.json because they have no datasheet doc, so the 'unique match' premise is false; (b) LS-C5K (Cat.5e UTP 8P8C, brass 3-prong, 50µ" gold, drawing MP11046) and LS-PASS-7UTP (pass-through 8P8C, 15µ" gold, drawing MP23022) are distinct SKUs with distinct drawings and plating, while the attestation is sample-specific ("applies only to the sample and its technical documentation submitted", applicant Cobtel Precision Electronics, Part No. 'UTP PLUG') — nothing ties that sample to either drawing; (c) Gu's blanket phrase 'all RJ45 connectors' is loose supplier speech naming no model and cannot license a model-level link.

Product type otherwise checks out for the revised link: unshielded (UTP) RJ45 8P8C modular plug / crystal head component, matching LS-CAT5E-UTP and LS-CAT6-UTP (BOR's UTP RJ45 connector line). Caveat to carry into the chatbot: despite the filename, this is a RoHS Attestation of Compliance (LCS211224020AR, 2022-01-06), not a CE Declaration of Conformity, and it covers the connector component only — it must not be handed out as the RoHS/CE certificate of a finished patch cord or LAN cable, nor for LS-CON44 (RJ11 6P4C), which it does not cover. sources.evidence:
The cited 2026 evidence is real but is NOT the best evidence, and the catalogue sweep is over-broad.

DIRECT ANCHOR FOUND (refutes the need for catalogue_match): the identical sha1 (238125 bytes) was already sent by BOR in an earlier thread — bodies.json key INBOX:14974, 2024-05-16, subject "Re: CE certificate for RJ45 connector", filename "FTP RJ45 connector-CE证书.pdf". Kyu's quoted 2024-05-14 request in that mail reads: "If you have CE certificate for RJ45 connector, Please send it. LS-CAT5E-UTP / CAT6-UTP / CAT6-STP..." and Gu replies "Please find attached CE certificate for UTP and FTP RJ45 connectors" with exactly two PDFs: the FTP one (this sha1) and the UTP twin (bc1de4b9a151da1330bf1966eadc4b04a57a4f7b). The shielded/FTP attestation therefore maps to the shielded model the customer named: LS-CAT6-STP. final_data.json already resolves this sha1 to ["LS-CAT6-STP"] at high confidence on exactly this basis; only the 2026 duplicate occurrence (INBOX:26438, the LS-CON44 RJ11 thread) landed in the retry queue.

PRODUCT TYPE MATCHES: doc is "Sample Name: Shielded crystal head / Part No.: FTP PLUG" (LCS220217076AR, 2022-02-28, applicant Cobtel Precision Electronics) = bare shielded 8P8C RJ45 modular plug. LS-CAT6-STP/LSN-CAT6-STP catalogue entry = "STP Cat.6 RJ45 Connector, 3 Clips, 15U" modular plug, sold as a standalone finished part. Same category, same shielding, same form factor, same connector.

WHY THE OTHER 5 FAMILIES FAIL:
1. Consistency test — the companion UTP attestation from the SAME mail, same lab, same applicant, was assigned narrowly to LS-CAT5E-UTP / LS-CAT6-UTP (the models named in the request) and was NOT swept across LS-C5K and LS-PASS-7UTP, which are equally valid UTP plug families in family_catalog_short.json. The FTP side must be scoped the same way; the 7-family sweep breaks the dataset's own convention.
2. LS-M850N is genuinely a DIFFERENT product type: "STP Cat.8 Modular Plug, Full Metal Shielded, Toolless / CAT8 Class I RJ45 plug to be assembled in the field", datasheet REV:A dated 2022-09 — seven months AFTER the 2022-02-28 cert. A full-metal toolless field-assembly plug is not a molded "crystal head". Handing an LS-M850N customer this certificate is exactly the wrong-certificate failure mode.
3. LS-EZ-750 already carries its own distinct RoHS from a different lab (SGS-CSTC, "RJ45 connector-ROHS.PDF") in final_data.json — it does not need and is not covered by this one.
4. LS-PASS-7STP, LS-CAT7-750, LS-CAT7-750G are plausible Cobtel siblings (Cobtel does hold the UL crystal-head certs that final_data links to LS-CAT7-750), but neither the document nor either mail thread names them. That is an inference chain, not evidence, and by the stated rule several families fitting equally makes the sweep too weak to ship.
5. The supplier's 2026 phrase "for all RJ45 connectors" is loose sales wording in a reply to an unrelated RJ11 (LS-CON44) request; the 2024 phrasing of the same attachment was the narrower "for UTP and FTP RJ45 connectors", i.e. scoped to the two categories the customer asked about.

CORRECTLY EXCLUDED: LS-CON44 (RJ11) — not in family_catalog_short.json and the document covers an RJ45 shielded plug, so RJ11 coverage is not demonstrated. The claim was right to leave it out.

LSN-CAT6-STP retained because family_catalog_short.json keys both codes to one identical datasheet ("LSN-CAT6-STP / LS-CAT6-STP, STP Cat.6 RJ45 커넥터 3 Clips·15µ\" 금도금, Rev.02, 2018-01-08") — the same physical part under two model designations, not a second product.

Minor caveat worth carrying to the chatbot (already in the record's caveat_ko): despite the filename, this is a RoHS Attestation of Compliance, not a CE Declaration of Conformity, and it covers the bare connector — it must not be served alone as the RoHS/CE certificate for a finished patch cord or LAN cable. [검증-수정] | 동일 파일이 다른 메일에서 이미 확정됨(중복 병합)

sources.subject: Re: CE certificate for DP / HDMI cable
sources.evidence:
This is not a catalogue-inference case. The identical attachment (sha1 38a4cfad..., DP线-RoHS证书.pdf, 530209 bytes) was sent by Gu TWICE, and the earlier mail names the model outright. bodies.json INBOX:14615 (2024-04-17, guzhiyi@bor-cable.com, subject "Re: COC for Display cable") body: "LS-DP192-xM series means DP to HDMI cable, so please find attached file." It replies to kyu's Sent:4586 (2024-04-16, "COC for Display cable"): "We need COC sheet for LS-DP192-xM series." Its two attachments are DP线-RoHS报告.pdf (b34cfa59a4dd = BCTC1912001252R) and DP线-RoHS证书.pdf (38a4cfad3be9 = BCTC1912001252C). The retry packet only surfaced the second, generic 2024-05-20 copy (INBOX:15025). final_data.json already files BOTH sha1s under model LS-DP192-XM (family LS-DP192), which is also why the LS-DP192 catalogue entry ends with the fragment "Sample name: DP CABLE series products / Testing type: DP to DP cable / Additional models:" — the claim cited that as "corroboration" when it is in fact the primary, direct evidence.

Why the proposed list is revised rather than confirmed:
(1) The claim's models array contains no LS-DP192-* code at all, i.e. it omits the one model the supplier explicitly named, while asserting the family. Concrete lengths from the LS-DP192-xM datasheet (enrichment.json, sha1 edc6ca51/e69353cf): LS-DP192-1M/1.5M/2M/3M/5M, DP1.2 male to HDMI1.4B male, 4K@30Hz, 30AWG OD6.0mm.
(2) The expansion is not principled. The certificate's Additional M/N list equally covers DP to DVI, DP to VGA, MINI DP to MINI DP, MINI DP to DVI/VGA, so LS-DP192-60H (DP1.4 male to HDMI2.0 male — the same category as LS-DP192) and the BOR-drawn LS-HD2DP-1M~5M / LS-HD2DPF-0.3M fit exactly as well as LS-DP14MM, yet are excluded. A scope list that broad selects nothing specific.
(3) Two supporting details are unsupported: family_catalog/final_data show LS-DP14MM-XM with an EMPTY issuer field (it is not documented as "BOR-drawn" as the claim states), and LS-DPFF-S0.2M is an F-F panel cable, which matches no literal entry on the certificate (the M-F "DP to DP EXTENSION CABLE" item is LS-DPMF-SXM).
(4) Positive counter-evidence against the expanded families: LS-DP12HD and LS-MDP12HD already carry DTI RoHS 2.0 report DTI201903158286-1 whose applicant is Ningbo SCPL Electronic Co., Ltd., and LS-DP14N carries HUAK/CER-MARK HK2506047299R + HK2506047299-1RR, also Ningbo SCPL. This certificate's manufacturer is Ningbo Borland Electronic Co., Ltd. Attaching a Borland-manufacturer RoHS certificate to models whose own filed RoHS is SCPL's risks handing a customer a different factory's document.

Factual corrections to the claim text: issue date is 2019-12-20 (not "2019-1"); the document is a RoHS Certificate of Compliance based on Directive 2011/65/EU + (EU) 2015/863 only, with no EMC (2014/30/EU) testing — relevant because the 2024-05-20 request was for a CE certificate, so this file alone does not answer an EMC-based CE request. It is also a text-layer-free scanned 1-page certificate and should be sent together with report BCTC1912001252R (b34cfa59a4dd). [검증-수정] | 동일 파일이 다른 메일에서 이미 확정됨(중복 병합)

Rendered the PDF (no text layer) and read it directly: certificate BCTC2003002134C, Applicant "Xiangshan Bor International Trade Co., Ltd", Manufacturer "Ningbo Borland Electronic Co., Ltd", Product "HDMI/DVI/VGA cable (with PVC/ABS/METAL housing)", Testing M/N "HDMI A male to HDMI A male", Additional M/N "HDMI A male to HDMI A female, HDMI A male to HDMI C male, HDMI A male to HDMI D male, HDMI A male to HDMI A male flat cable, HDMI to DVI cable, HDMI to VGA cable, DVI to DVI cable, DVI to VGA cable, VGA to VGA cable", RoHS 2011/65/EU + (EU)2015/863, valid only for report BCTC2003002134R, Apr 01 2020. So the cited scope is real, and the applicant is exactly the thread's counterpart (guzhiyi@bor-cable.com), who sent it unprompted in answer to kyu's generic "CE certificate for DP / HDMI cable" request.

CONFIRMED PARTS. Every proposed family is a BOR-drawn passive copper assembly whose connector pairing is named on the certificate, verified against BOR datasheets in final_data.json: LS-HDMT (BOR drawings LS-HDMT-0.3-5M / 10M-15M / 20M, HDMI A-A metal) = Testing M/N; LS-SHD20 (BOR "Slim HDMI cable.pdf", HDMI 2.0 slim A-A, CUSTOMER: LANstar) = Testing M/N; LS-DVI19M-HDMI (BOR, "HDMI MALE TO DVI 18+1 MALE") = "HDMI to DVI cable"; LS-DVI19M (DVI 18+1 M-M) and LS-DVI25M (DVI 24+1 M-M), both from guzhiyi@bor-cable.com INBOX:5382 = "DVI to DVI cable"; LS-RGB-15MM (BOR S-VGA RGB3+4 HDB15 M/M) and LS-RGB-15MF (BOR HDB15 M-F extension) = "VGA to VGA cable". Independent corroboration: the companion report BCTC2003002134R (sha1 aad348582b) is already attached at high confidence to LS-HDMT-XM (kyu asked ROHS II for LS-HDMT-xM by model name, INBOX:12468) and to LS-DVI25M-XM (verified=confirm). Active/optical BOR products are correctly excluded (LS-HDMI-2MM and LS-HDMI-EXT carry repeater ICs; LS-HDAOC/LS-H20AOC are AOC) — the certificate covers only passive PVC/ABS/METAL-housing cable.

REFUTED RATIONALE (conclusion survives). The claim maps "HDMI to VGA -> LS-HRGB-15MM". That is wrong: the BOR drawing 7e6b50f373 "LS-HRGB-15MM.pdf" reads "VGA3+6 HDB15M/HDB15M", a high-spec VGA male-to-male monitor cable (RGB 3+6 coax, UL AWM 2990, LANstar print). LS-HRGB is the 3+6 grade of LS-RGB's 3+4, not an HDMI converter. It stays in the list, but under "VGA to VGA cable". No Lanstar family in this archive matches "HDMI to VGA" or "DVI to VGA".

WHY REVISE. The certificate's first Additional M/N, "HDMI A male to HDMI A female", is LS-HDMI-HMF — BOR drawing "LS-HDMI-HMF 0.15-5M.pdf" (sha1 2ae5e1aef9), "HDMI AM TO HDMI AF CABLE V2.0 19+1", passive, PVC/metal. Its companion report BCTC2003002134R is already linked to LS-HDMI-HMF-XM at HIGH confidence (INBOX:3573: kyu requested RoHS for LS-HDMI-HMF-xm by model code and Gu replied with that very report; that doc's own caveat says "RoHS 요청 시에는 BCTC2003002134R 성적서를 별도로 보내야 합니다"). Attaching the report half to LS-HDMI-HMF but withholding the certificate half would make the chatbot unable to answer a CE request for that model. Added LS-HDMI-HMF, plus LS-HDMT-20M (BOR drawing, sha1 035e767623, same family, arbitrarily dropped) and LS-DVI19M-HDMI-15M/-20M (BOR drawings d27fe47a96 / 6737b85fff, same family).

CAVEAT for the chatbot: this is a RoHS-based CE certificate only — no EMC/LVD testing. EMC CE for HDMI is a different document (Qstlab Qst-22N070162E). Weakest member of the set is LS-SHD20, whose drawing (2020-12-18, 34AWG tinned-copper, OD 3.8mm) postdates the certificate and differs in construction from the tested sample, though it matches the certified model designation exactly. sources.subject: for slim patch cord and flat patch
sources.evidence:
EVIDENCE VERIFIED. r_008.json contains the doc. Cert text: "Product Name: Network flat lan cable / Model/Type Reference: Network flat patch cord / CAT.5E, CAT.6, CAT.6A, CAT.7, CAT.8.1 / U,UTP…S,FTP / PVC…TERYLENE / all colours / MALE TO MALE, MALE TO FEMALE", applicant+manufacturer Xiangshan Bor International Trade, EN 55032/55035, 2026-05-26. No LS code anywhere. Mail INBOX:27456 (guzhiyi@bor-cable.com -> kyu, 2026-07-08 07:54:20, "for slim patch cord and flat patch") says only "Please also find attached certificats for slim patch cord and flat patch cord"; quoted request lists LS-6UTPD/6UTPC/6STPD/USB-AMBM/5UTPAD.

NEGATIVE CONTROL PASSES. INBOX:27455, sent 07:53:13 — one minute before — carried BCTC2511421501CN1/RN1 (RoHS) + BCTC2511748719C/E (CE-EMC) for "Network cable", i.e. the round set that actually answers those five requested models (manifest confirms 2511748719C is filed to LS-5UTPAD/6UTPC/6UTPD/6STPD/6SFTP-300M/6FTP-100MG/HF705). So 27456 is a genuine extra covering the flat and slim lines, and the five quoted models are correctly excluded (catalogue confirms 6UTPD/6UTPC/6STPD/5UTPAD = round patch cords, USB-AMBM = USB). The packet also contains the separate slim cert BCTC2511173018C, so flat/slim are not conflated. Slim families (LS-BFTP7 "Slim Easy Bent U/FTP Cat.6A", LS-SL6, LS-6AUTP, LS-6AFTP) and LS-5FTPSD (Cat.5e panel cable) are correctly kept out.

PRODUCT TYPE MATCHES for all five proposed families — manifest.jsonl titles: 문서/LS-F6-UTPD-XM_Datasheet_Flat U-UTP Cat.6 Patch Cord.pdf; LS-F7-UTPD-XM_Datasheet ("플랫 U/UTP CAT.6A/7 패치코드, 30AWG, OD 1.45x6.05mm"); LS-F7FTP-XM_Datasheet ("32AWG Cat.6A U/FTP 플랫 패치코드", T2022042001); LS-F8FTP-XXM_Datasheet ("플랫 U/FTP CAT.8", 2025-07-04); LS-FT6UXXM_Datasheet ("CAT.6 U/UTP 플랫 패치코드 투명"). All BOR-issued. Corroborating mails exist (INBOX:16472/16533 "Flat patch cord"; INBOX:15891/Sent:5001 "ROHS / MSDS sheet for Flat cable"; INBOX:21066 where Gu identifies Kyu's "LS-H8FTP" as "It's Flat Cat.8 patch cords" and then issues the LS-F8FTP datasheet).

REASON FOR REVISE — the set is under-inclusive by three catalogue keys that are the same flat product, so those model codes would get nothing:
(1) LS-F6UTPD — distinct family key, members LS-F6UTPD-0.5MW…-20MW (white flat Cat.6); the archive's own flat datasheet carries families ['LS-F6-UTPD','LS-F6UTPD'].
(2) LS-FT6UXXM — distinct family key; 문서/LS-FT6UXXM_Datasheet_LS-FT6UxxM.pdf has families ['LS-FT6UXXM'] while the Fluke reports for the same series sit under 'LS-FT6U'.
(3) LS-F7-SFTP — live family key (members LS-F7-SFTP-XM/XXM), proven FLAT twice in mail: Kyu 2021-03-12 subject "ROHS sheet about cat.7 SFTP flat cable" body "could you please send the ROHS sheet about LS-F7-SFTP-Xm"; Gu 2021-10-15 "2) As for item Flat U/FTP Cat.6A patch cord ( LS-F7-SFTP-xM)". The claim demotes it to a mere former name of LS-F7FTP and drops it.

Multi-family fan-out is the archive convention for BOR scope-level certificates: BCTC2511748719C sits on 7 families with wildcard models (LS-6UTPD-*M …), and BCTC-FYC19010403C/R sits on 8-9 families and already includes LS-F7-SFTP. Confidence medium, not high: the link is scope/product-type based, no Lanstar code appears in the certificate, so delivery must carry the caveat that the cert names only BOR's generic "Network flat patch cord" range. [검증-수정]

The five models in kyu's quoted RoHS/MSDS request (LS-6UTPD, LS-6UTPC, LS-6STPD, LS-USB-AMBM, LS-5UTPAD) are round cords / USB and are not the subject of this report. [검증완료]

sources.subject: RE: HDMI keystone for ROHS
sources.evidence:
HALF THE CLAIM IS RIGHT FOR THE WRONG REASON, HALF IS TOO WEAK.

(1) File identity: this exact sha1 was attached to THREE mails, byte-identical (verified with shasum on attachments_raw/INBOX_6376/"ROHS Report.pdf", INBOX_10694/"ROHS Report.pdf", INBOX_3758/"ROHS Test Report(106-09-06).pdf" — all 5ed5e41b44b030ad6aec627e9bd6eb77856dadf5). So the link does not have to rest on catalogue similarity at all; there is direct supplier evidence.

(2) LS-GIC-FKTMT — CONFIRMED by supplier's own words, not by catalogue. bodies.json INBOX:6376 (Roy, 2022-01-18, "RE: C.O.C Sheet", answering kyu 2022-01-17 "C.O.C sheet about below product? 1. LS-GIC-FKTMT"): "Please kindly receive attached ROHS report / GIC-FKTMT30Z-38 (LS-GIC-FKTMT) Is compliant with 2011/65/EU and Amendment (EU) 2015/863 / Please refer to page 2 XICX-XXXXX". This report's conclusion is exactly "2011/65/EU and Amendment (EU) 2015/863" and its p.2 Series No. block ends with "Inline Coupler Model XICX-XXXXX". Exact fit.

(3) LS-GIC-UJW — CONFIRMED. INBOX:10694 (Roy, 2023-05-18) attaches this same file replying to kyu's "Could you please send UL sheet (include LS-GIC-UJW) and ROHS sheet?": "For ROHS report, please kindly refer to page 2" = the Inline Coupler XICX-XXXXX entry. GIC-UJW matches XICX-XXXXX with X=G. Same category/construction (Cat.6A RJ45 inline coupler, keystone-type).

(4) LS-7PLB-F24X and LS-BZ-KTBKZ — REFUTED as non-specific. I extracted the full 13-page PDF with pypdf. The Series No. declaration (pp.2-4) covers essentially the WHOLE EPNew line: Patch Panel (xPLxx-, ISDN-, XPx89-, xxPLKx-), Keystone Jack (xKTxxx-), Mount Box, Inline Coupler (xICx-), PCB Module Wall Outlet (xA-/xBx-/xCx-/xDx-/xFx-/xGx-), Snap accessories SNP-, Unloaded Patch Panel PLKx-, Cable Manager/Rack PLMNx-/RACKx-, 89 Bracket, Universal Empty Box, Faceplates & Back Box, MultiMedia Keystone Insert KSRx-, T MOD Adaptor xTMD-, LAN Cable Tester LT-, LAN Cable CBLC-, Patch Cord CBL-, Plug P-/6PG-/PLUG-SOS45X/LKPG-45NYXXZ, Boot BOOT-, Bezel BZ-XXX, Cable Tie, Tool, Key, Dust Cover. family_catalog.json contains 25 EPNew-sourced families and ALL of them fall inside this list. So "inside the declared series" discriminates nothing: LS-BZ-KTWHZ (bezel, white) fits identically to LS-BZ-KTBKZ, and LS-GPLB-F24X / LS-6PLB-24P19N / LS-EPLB-24P19N / LS-6PLB-48P19 / LS-EPLB-48P19 fit identically to LS-7PLB-F24X, as do LS-ETMD-UJWT (T MOD), LS-LKPG SERIES (Plug), LS-GKTVNL-U1WH/-F1MT (Keystone Jack), LS-6IC-UJW/LS-EIC-UJW/LS-GIC-FJM/LS-6IC-UK etc. (Inline Coupler). The claim's own support for those two is that they carry "sister" reports — but that sister is a DIFFERENT document (REACH 223 - 2022.pdf, Intertek SVHC TWNC01059836, sha1 01c5d38814b6c96ab91b6f43eeb5c09c95e8b607), never this RoHS report. Attaching a patch-panel/bezel label to this file on that basis is unprincipled and would let the chatbot serve it for dozens of other families equally.

(5) The claim's core "verbatim 260/260 catalogue match" is partly circular: family_catalog_short.json is one representative doc per family, and for LS-GIC-FKTMT / LS-GIC-UJW that representative IS this very file (final_data.json already records docs[5ed5e41b].models = ["LS-GIC-FKTMT","LS-GIC-UJW"]). It is not independent corroboration — but the underlying mail bodies are, so the conclusion survives for those two.

(6) On the literal thread request (INBOX:3758 / Sent 2021-03-03, "we need ROHS sheet about HDMI keystone jack"): Roy's reply "It is in 'MultiMedia Keystone Insert' series" is factually correct — p.3 of this report declares "MultiMedia Keystone Insert Model KSRX-XXXXXX… followed KSR the first X is either WH, BK or blank". But there is no Lanstar KSR family: grepping family_catalog.json for KSR/MultiMedia/멀티미디어/Keystone Insert returns zero families; the only KSR strings in the archive are LS-LKSR-BK / LS-LKSR-WT (PI-LS0624202501.pdf, PI0202202101rev.2.pdf) which are "Lock Insert, For RJ45" (LKSR-45NY...), a different product and not the KSRx- pattern; LSP-6KTVM-F1MT / LSP-GKTVM-F1MT / LS-GKTVNL-* are RJ45 Cat.6/6A keystone jacks, not HDMI. So no HDMI/multimedia family can honestly be added for that mail instance.

CONCLUSION: keep LS-GIC-FKTMT and LS-GIC-UJW (backed by Roy's explicit per-model statements about this exact PDF, page-2 XICX-XXXXX); drop LS-7PLB-F24X and LS-BZ-KTBKZ (blanket-series membership only, dozens of other families fit equally well, different product categories — patch panel and bezel vs inline coupler).

sources.subject: HDMI, DP premium cable
sources.evidence: Thread: kyu asks BOR (Gu) to develop premium HDMI/DP cables because margins on 'existing cables (HD21, DP14)' are too thin; on 2024-09-11 Gu attaches this licence with 'HDMI 2.1 cable is no problem, please see attached certificate and testing'. The project was postponed on 2024-11-11 ('we will need to raise funds... contact you again early next year'), so no new LS code was ever issued in this thread. The link is made through the licensee identity: the catalogue shows LS-HD21's HDMI Forum ATC Certificate of Confirmation lists Adopter = Ningbo SCPL Electronics Co., Ltd. (parent model SCPL-001-5M, HDMI 2.1 5m 28AWG), and LS-HDMI21's DTI RoHS report (DTI201903158286-10) names Ningbo SCPL Electronic as applicant. So this adopter licence is the company-level HDMI licence of the very factory that certifies/manufactures Lanstar's HDMI 2.1 cable families. [검증완료]

sources.subject: Re: Serial cable ROHS sheet
sources.evidence:
Cited serial evidence is genuine but the claim's scope is wrong on three counts.

(1) MISSING THE STRONGEST LINK — VGA. The identical sha1 261433ec was first attached in INBOX:5014 (2021-08-13, "Re: ROHS2"), answering Sent:1707 where kyu names a Lanstar model code explicitly: "we need the ROHS2 sheet for LS-SRGB-15MM-Xm". Gu: "Please find attached SGS test report of ROHS for VGA cables!". The 2021-09-03 serial pack (INBOX:5210) is that same VGA pack minus one file — all 9 remaining sha1s are identical (ALUMINUM FOIL df4ca43b, C2680 d93ccd60, COPPER WIRE 261433ec, FERRITE RING 3ff9a0f4, FOAMED db96b4ac, LCP 5ead0954, PVC efdec526, SCREW 9f7d594b, SPCC fdb8f31e); only AL-MG ALLOY WIRE ecce97ea was dropped. "LS-SRGB-15MM" (string occurs only in Sent:1707/INBOX:5014) maps to catalogue family LS-RGB-15MM, whose entry begins "S-VGA CABLE (RGB 3+4), M/M — LS-RGB-15MM-1M/1.8M/.../30M". That is a direct model-coded link, stronger than the inferred serial one, and the claim omits it entirely.

(2) LS-SER-9MFC WRONGLY EXCLUDED. INBOX:5212 (2021-09-03, same day as the RoHS pack) delivered LS-SER-9FF-xxM.pdf AND LS-SER-9MFC-xxM.pdf; INBOX:6082 (2021-12-12, "DATA sheet of New Supplier") attaches the full BOR serial line as Lanstar codes: DB25M-DB9F-3C+1-2M.pdf, LS-SER-9F25M-1.8M.pdf, LS-SER-9FF.pdf, LS-SER-9MF.pdf, LS-SER-9MFC.pdf, LS-SER-9MM.pdf, LS-SER-25MF.pdf, LS-SER-25MM.pdf. LS-SER-9MFC is a distinct catalogue family. Including 9F25M-1.8M (not delivered in the Aug/Sep thread) while dropping 9MFC (delivered in it) is arbitrary.

(3) CONSTRUCTION ARGUMENT IS FALSE AS STATED. The claim asserts the LS-SER drawings have a bare-copper (BC) drain. Catalogue: LS-SER-9MF/9MM/9FF/9MFC/25MF/25MM all specify 7/0.12 CCS x nC + 7/0.12 CCS drain + AL foil + PVC — CCS drain, not BC. Only LS-SER-9F25M-1.8M (Xinya current drawing) has 7/0.12CCA x 6C + 7/0.12BC drain. Bare copper fits the VGA cable far better: LS-RGB-15MM = [(7/0.12BC+FPE)+7/0.12CCS+AL]x3C + 7/0.12CCS x4C + AL + 7/0.12CCS drain. Corroborating that the pack is VGA-origin: it still contains FERRITE MAGNETIC RING, FOAMED MATERIAL and LCP, which belong to the VGA/monitor cable (2 ferrite cores, foamed-PE coax) and have no counterpart in the RS-232 drawings. The 2022-07-27 genuine new-supplier serial pack (INBOX:7770) instead contains Conductor(CCS), Contact Pin, H62, PBT — and no copper wire at all.

Serial attachment context is nevertheless real and supplier-vouched: Sent:1784 asks "ROHS sheet for Serial cable"; INBOX:5210 answers with this file and "Actually serial cable material is same as VGA cable marerial"; the parallel REACH pack INBOX:5320 answers Sent:1820, which names LS-SER-25MM-1.8M, with the same material list including Copper Wire-REACH.PDF. So the serial families belong on the list — all seven of them — alongside the VGA family the report was originally issued for.

Confidence medium: this is a raw-material (copper wire, LANXI DECHEN, SGS SHAEC2022912502) sheet with no product code, inherently shared across BOR's D-sub cable line; the listed set is exactly the set the supplier attached it to.

sources.subject: Re: Serial cable ROHS sheet
sources.evidence:
EVERY cited item verified verbatim against the raw archive, none paraphrased.

1) Delivery context is unambiguous and supplier-attested. Sent:1784 (2021-09-03 06:35 UTC, kyu -> guzhiyi@bor-cable.com, subj "Serial cable ROHS sheet") = "Could you please send the ROHS sheet for Serial cable?". INBOX:5210 (2021-09-03 07:52 UTC) replies with exactly 9 material SGS reports incl. C2680-ROHS.PDF (verified in /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/mails/cand_INBOX_5210.eml attachment list) and the remark "Actually serial cable material is same as VGA cable marerial." So BOR consciously supplied this pack AS the serial cable's RoHS dossier. The link is supplier-attested, not inferred.

2) "Serial cable" in kyu<->Gu vocabulary = the LS-SER line, proven three independent ways:
- Sent:1763 (2021-08-30, subj "Serial cable data sheet"): "9FF , 9MM , 25MM , 25MF , 9F25M" plus the existing "Serial MF" sheet (attachments SERIAL-9FF.pdf, "serial MF cable.PNG").
- Gu answered that request with PDFs literally named with Lanstar codes: INBOX:5193 (2021-09-01) LS-SER-25MF-xxM.pdf + LS-SER-25MM-xxM.pdf; INBOX:5201 (2021-09-02) LS-SER-9MF-xxM.pdf + LS-SER-9MM-xxM.pdf; INBOX:5212 (2021-09-03, SAME DAY as the RoHS pack) LS-SER-9FF-xxM.pdf + LS-SER-9MFC-xxM.pdf.
- Sent:1820 (2021-09-15): "Reach or MSDS sheet for serial cable (LS-SER-25MM-1.8M )" — kyu equates the words to a Lanstar code himself, 12 days later, same supplier.
Line still live in 2026 (Sent:6852 / INBOX:25881, "DB 25pin serial cables" from JieXun).

3) Product-type match is real: C2680 is brass strip for connector shell/contact parts; family_catalog_short.json describes every LS-SER family as a D-sub assembly with "금도금 핀, 니켈도금 쉘" (gold-plated pins over brass, nickel-plated shell). Same category, same construction, same connector family.

WHY REVISE, not confirm: the catalogue contains exactly seven LS-SER families — LS-SER-9MF, 9MFC, 9FF, 9MM, 25MF, 25MM, 9F25M-1.8M. The claim lists six and drops LS-SER-9MFC (DB9M<->DB9F crossover/null-modem, 7C+1, drawing QJ/XYT-A200900). That omission is an artifact of copying kyu's Aug-30 shopping list; Gu's own reply delivered LS-SER-9MFC-xxM.pdf on 2021-09-03, the very day of this RoHS pack, and kyu's request ("ROHS sheet for Serial cable") was line-wide with no model restriction. Same supplier, same week, same brass shells — excluding 9MFC would be arbitrary. Added.

DELIBERATE EXCLUSION (checked, rejected): LS-GEN-DB9FF (mini gender changer) is a BOR D-sub product with the same brass, but it is not a cable and was handled in a separate thread (Sent:1972 / INBOX:5837, "serial gender", Nov 2021). Kept out.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS AND WHY THEY FAIL:
- "Generic raw-material report, not product-specific." True but not disqualifying: kb_docs.json shows this identical sha1 (size 371580) already resolved to VGA models LS-HRGB-15MM-XM / LS-SRGB-15MM-XM via INBOX:8658 ("Re: ROHS for High VGA cable", 2022-11-14) and INBOX:5014 ("Re: ROHS2", 2021-08-13). So the file is genuinely shared across product lines — which is exactly what Gu said would happen. Being non-exclusive makes it multi-attributed, not mis-attributed. This packet resolves the INBOX:5210 (serial) instance; the VGA instance is already recorded separately. A customer asking for LS-SER RoHS receives precisely the document BOR issued for LS-SER.
- "Codes borrowed from a different thread" (the previous_reason for marking it unresolved). The 'different thread' is the same buyer, same supplier, same product word, same week, and one of its deliveries lands on the same calendar day. That is the archive-wide family resolution the task explicitly sanctions, not a leap.
- "Would a different family fit equally well?" Only the VGA families LS-RGB/LS-HRGB/LS-SRGB, and only because Gu said so — and those are already separately attributed to this sha1. No other Lanstar family is a competing candidate for THIS mail.

Residual caveat (does not change the verdict): this is the OLD-supplier dossier. Kyu asked for a new-factory RoHS 2.0 on 2022-07-22 (Sent:2742) and Gu delivered a replacement pack on 2022-07-27 (INBOX:7770). A chatbot serving current LS-SER RoHS should prefer the 2022 pack; this 2021 file remains valid evidence for pre-2022 production.

sources.subject: Re: Serial cable ROHS sheet
sources.evidence:
REFUTED. The LS-SER catalogue guess is wrong; the document has direct named-model evidence pointing to VGA cable.

1) THE FILE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL IN THREE MAILS. shasum -a 1 over scratchpad/attachments_raw gives db96b4acddbc9bb21d36689c9f9fe71fef0aed32 for all of: INBOX_5014/"FOMAED MATERIAL-ROHS.PDF", INBOX_5210/"FOMAED MATERIAL-ROHS.PDF" (the serial thread the claim used), INBOX_8658/"Fomaed material-ROHS.PDF". Two of those three threads DO name a Lanstar model, in kyu's own request text:
 - INBOX:5014 (2021-08-13) kyu: "we need the ROHS2 sheet for LS-SRGB-15MM-Xm)" -> BOR guzhiyi: "Please find attached SGS test report of ROHS for VGA cables!" (10 attachments incl. this file).
 - INBOX:8658 (2022-11-14) kyu subject "ROHS for High VGA cable.": "We need ROHS sheet about LS-HRGB-15MM-Xm." -> BOR: "Please find attached SGS test report for VGA cables." (9 attachments incl. this file).
So the document is not model-less at all; the first pass only looked at the serial thread. final_data.json already carries this sha1 with models ["LS-HRGB-15MM-XM","LS-SRGB-15MM-XM"], both sources marked confidence "high", and a caveat_ko stating it is a VGA-cable raw material sheet.

2) THE PRODUCT TYPE IS NOT THE SAME. The sample is a foamed insulation compound (yellow grains, Guangzhou Kingsens, client-ref grades KS 208 / KS 3105-4200 = coax/VGA foam grades). Every LS-SER family in family_catalog.json is a solid construction: "CCS + 0.12CCS 드레인와이어 + 알루미늄 포일 + PVC 자켓" (LS-SER-9MM/9MF/9FF/9MFC OD 4.5mm, LS-SER-25MM/25MF OD 6.90mm, LS-SER-9F25M OD 4.0mm), with LD-PE appearing only as mold-hood material, never as foamed core insulation. VGA 3+4 cable (LS-RGB/LS-SRGB/LS-HRGB, HDB15) does have 3 foam-insulated mini-coax cores. Category, construction and connector all mismatch for LS-SER.

3) THE GENUINE SERIAL BOM PACK CONTAINS NO FOAM. Later in the same thread kyu asked for ROHS2.0 for serial cable from the new factory (2022-07-22); BOR delivered INBOX:7770 (2022-07-27) whose attachments are exactly: Aluminum Foil, Conductor(CCS), Contact Pin, H62, PBT, PVC, SPCC. Foamed material is absent. That is BOR's own itemisation of the serial cable's materials and it excludes this sheet.

4) THE CLAIM'S ONLY SUPPORT IS BOR'S BLANKET LINE. "Actually serial cable material is same as VGA cable marerial" is an admission that BOR re-sent the VGA material pack unchanged, not evidence that foam is in the serial cable. The claim's own confidence note concedes foam is in no LS-SER drawing.

5) UNIQUENESS TEST. Restricting to the two families is justified by the model codes kyu typed, not by catalogue similarity. On construction alone LS-RGB-15MM / LS-RGB-15MF (BOR VGA 3+4, OD 7.0/8.0mm) would fit equally well, so they are deliberately NOT asserted here - no mail ties this sha1 to them. Conversely no honest reading puts a DB9/DB25 serial family on a foamed-insulation sheet.

CAVEAT for the chatbot: this remains a raw-material (원자재) RoHS report - applicant is Guangzhou Kingsens, not Lanstar or BOR, and no LS code appears inside the PDF. Serve it only as one component sheet alongside the rest of the VGA BOM pack (PVC, SPCC, LCP, C2680, Aluminum foil, Copper wire, Ferrite, Screw), never alone as a finished-product RoHS certificate.
